<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **68** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getDiagnosed (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via attachClusterPubSub (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MemoryLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via resolveWritePackageScope (literal, a string literal in getMetaItemLayered))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1326aba0bec24847557a3a22d650bedb7ad89284` — the merge of head `46c2cab0b5bee77e6368631eaf1c98e2bd3afa38` into base `d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1326aba0bec24847557a3a22d650bedb7ad89284 && git checkout 1326aba0bec24847557a3a22d650bedb7ad89284
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41 46c2cab0b5bee77e6368631eaf1c98e2bd3afa38 && git checkout -B drift-repro d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41 && git merge --no-ff 46c2cab0b5bee77e6368631eaf1c98e2bd3afa38

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d728d73e6d5d4b21b0a5eaeaef59c968a794ec41` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a309114bf448808c476e64a349a420053c422c20`
Local-runs: probe — round 1 on this head was dispatched with an ablation and a declaration check that the diff and check-runs alone cannot answer; runs listed under "Runs" below
Scope: .changeset/32560-bare-action-read-loader-slots.md, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-action-slots.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts + packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts (not in the diff; read, since row 5b makes a claim about both)

Round 1 on this head. Diff read at the merge base `9cd5fc161` (`git diff origin/main...a309114bf`, 9 files, +696/−64). Card #32560, seat ruling 6817582700 (items 1, 2, 2', 3, 4, 5a, 5b), row 6 from #32551's third review, os-dev-report 6822928487.

### ① Derived judgments

Each FROM → TO row against the code and its pin:

| row | true against the code | pin asserts it | red when the change is put back |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 in process (409 `[A, platform]`) | yes: `judgesLoaderSlots` → `loadSlottedDiagnosed` → `platformSlotsOf` → `refuseAcrossOwners` | yes (candidates, status, code, "2 holders", the platform sentence, on `get` and `getDiagnosed`) | yes |
| 1 served, 3 (both arms) | yes: `rethrowPackageScopedRefusal` hands back the dropped refusal, `judgeDroppedServiceRefusal` judges it, plain read and `/layers` code layer | yes | yes |
| 2, 2' | yes | yes | yes |
| 4 wording | yes (`counted` in `packageScopedRefusalMessage`) | yes | yes |
| 5a | yes for A, B + environment | yes (removal candidates equal the read's) | yes |
| 5b beside the platform's item | yes | yes | yes |
| 5b beside the environment's item | **not in the door + database shape** — F1 | only with one loader holding both items | yes for the pinned shape |
| 6 | yes (`servedFromDisabledHolder`, both reads) | yes | yes |

Ablation, each change put back alone, the `[#32560]` pins re-run, then restored (final tree clean, pins green: metadata 15/15, runtime file 63/63):

- `judgesLoaderSlots` returns false (the registry alone answers, the old read): 4 red (items 1, 2, 2', 4).
- `storeRemovalKeys` without the package-less-only return (a bare removal takes every slot): 4 red (5b × 2 in each of the two files).
- `platformSlotsOf` returns the empty set: 2 red (item 1, 5b beside the platform's item).
- `packageScopedRefusalMessage` counting as before: 2 red (item 4, the three-holder removal).
- `judgeDroppedServiceRefusal` returns `undefined` (metadata-protocol rebuilt): 3 red in the runtime file (item 3 both arms, item 1 through the protocol).
- `servedFromDisabledHolder` returns false (rebuilt): 1 red (row 6).

Findings:

- **F1 · must-fix (correctness; a declared TO that the code does not give).** Row 5b and changeset §4 / BREAKING 4 say a removal naming no package beside one package "takes the environment's own item only (its registry slot, the door's copy and its package-less rows); the package's action stays". The manager judges the keys over registry ∪ loaders, but each loader then applies `storeRemovalKeys` to its OWN slots (`MemoryLoader.delete`, `DatabaseLoader.delete`, called with no package by `deleteMetaItemFromLoader`). In the artifact door's boot (the shape `metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts` documents: the door's `MemoryLoader` holds the package bodies, `DatabaseLoader` holds the rows) the door holds A alone, so its "one holder, every slot" arm deletes A's copy. Measured on this head with that boot plus an environment row and its registry slot: before, door `[alpha]`, rows `[A, null]`, bare read `env`; after `unregister('action', NAME)`: door `[]`, rows `[A]`, registry list `[alpha]`. A manager over the door alone then answers nothing for the name. `removeNodeLocalCopies` runs the same loader delete on every cluster peer. On `main` the same call removed A everywhere, so this is no loosening and no new loss against `main`; it is the new rule not reaching one of the stores the row names, and the registry and the door now disagree about A. The `[#32560]` pins use one loader that holds both items, so they stay green. Either carry the manager's judgment to the loaders (a loader that holds only the package's item deletes nothing on a removal judged package-less-only) with a pin on the door + database boot, or state the door's behaviour in the row and the changeset and carry the fix on a follow-up card; the seat picks.
- **F2 · should-fix.** A, B and the platform's item (registered only): the bare read is refused naming `[A, B, platform]`; the bare removal is refused naming `[A, B, environment]` with "The environment's own item binds it to object …". `removalOf` first calls `storeRemovalKeys` on the registry with no platform keys, and with two packages that call throws before the registry ∪ loaders view is judged. The removal is still refused and removes nothing; the candidate kind and the sentence differ from the read's, against the ruling's "naming the same candidates". No pin covers this shape.
- **F3 · should-fix (read in the code, not measured).** Execution face: where the metadata service holds A's item and a package-less item it only registers, `MetadataManager.get` now refuses `[A, platform]`; `rethrowPackageScopedRefusal` drops it (one enabled package) and `readMetaItem` judges the dropped refusal on the served face only, so the execution read falls through to the registry step where it took the service's package-less item before. The body and the changeset declare the served reads only. Measure it and either declare the row or keep the old answer.
- **F4 · should-fix.** On the new path a loader that throws leaves `platformKeys` unset and the loaders' holders unseen, and `getDiagnosed` answers `degraded: false` with `errors` filled (measured: A and a package-less slot in memory, the one loader throwing → the package-less item, `degraded: false`). The answer is the old one, as the changeset says, but the read now depends on the loaders and reports a judgment it could not complete as complete (ADR-0110 D3). Same for the removal: with the loader down it takes the package-less slot.
- **F5 · nit.** `judgeDroppedServiceRefusal` lists every action of the service to find one name; `servedFromDisabledHolder` compares by `JSON.stringify`. Both sit on rare paths.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is present, line-initial, in the PR body and the changeset; the narrowing arm is true and its FROM → TO rows are there (rows 1, 2', 3 without the row, 5b beside the platform's item). **F6 · should-fix:** the value `yes` declares a widening, and neither the line nor the table names one: every other row is a moved answer at the same status or a removal that takes less. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: "`yes (narrowing)` — a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; "`no (narrowing)` — NOT a widening, but breaking". Name the widening or write `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (PR body and changeset). The arm, the BREAKING banner and the review tier are the same either way.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**, and `patch` follows from it. Governing text, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: "`Metadata-protocol: added|narrowed|semantic|none`, the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key, accepted value or metadata type is `added`; a key removed or tombstoned, a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`; a changed meaning or default is `semantic`; all else is `none`", and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The pm-dispatch claim template says the same: "the kind of change to what a metadata author can write". The diff touches no schema, no key, no accepted value, no metadata type and no write path (`storeWriteKeys` and the write refusal are untouched; `packages/spec` is not in the diff). What moves is the answer of a by-name read and of a removal that name no package: a 200 → 409 on `GET /meta/action/NAME`, its `/layers`, `MetadataManager.get` / `getDiagnosed` / `unregister`. That is a narrowing of an answer, which is the Clause-② arm's subject, not the authoring surface's (the ruling relayed from #32649: the line declares the authoring surface only). The first declaration, `narrowed`, was the wrong one; the ADR-0087 gate was right to ask it for a semantic migration entry, since #32649 refuses `no-migration-prescription` on a declared `narrowed`, and there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite here. Merged PR #32551 declared `Metadata-protocol: none` beside `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` for the same class of move (bare action read 200 → 409) and shipped with a `no-migration-prescription` disposition.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `patch`; the `!` subject, the **BREAKING** block with four FROM → TO lines and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are present. `@objectstack/runtime` changes a test only. BREAKING line 4 inherits F1.
- `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is present, as a `(narrowing)` arm owes it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` path, no generated artifact, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no `content/docs/releases/**`, no `skills/**` in the diff. 696 added lines, under the 3000-line line.
- No security item found in this diff.
- Cost: one `loaderSlotsNamed` per bare action read that hits a package's slot in memory, as the ruling accepted and the body states.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing against the published contract on `main`: ADR-0150 D3 answers a caller with no package by the environment's own item, then the unique package holder, else a refusal naming every candidate. Rows 1, 2' and 3 make that refusal real where the read picked (the platform's item beside a package; one of two packages); rows 2, 3 and 6 move the answer to the holder the rule names. None takes a declared capability away: every refused read has the package-addressed form the refusal prescribes. No resolution loosens.
- `package-slotted-store.ts` / `metadata-manager.ts`: the read side agrees with the rule and with the protocol's judge (`platform` = a package-less slot no loader stores; the protocol tells it by the environment's active row; in production both read `sys_metadata`). The removal side agrees in the registry and in a loader that holds both items, and not across loaders (F1), nor in the candidate kind beside two packages (F2).
- `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` / `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`: the dropped refusal is judged only when it names a package-less holder and the service lists exactly one such item; otherwise the read goes on as before. `servedFromDisabledHolder` is read only when a judged answer is set and the service's answer is package-less. Both agree with the rows they implement; the execution face is F3.

### Runs

In a detached worktree at the head, dependencies built with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1` (`packages/spec` prepare failed on the tsx socket path; the migration registry was built by hand):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata exec vitest run`: exit 1 · 1506 passed, 1 failed. The one failure is `typescript-serializer-annotation.test.ts` (TS7016, no `.d.ts`), an effect of `OS_SKIP_DTS=1` here, not of the diff.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run`: exit 0 · 22738 passed / 36 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run`: exit 0 · 3439 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`: exit 0 · 63 passed.
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0 (one declared-breaking changeset, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
- Check-runs on the head, read: all listed runs `success`.
- Not run: the full `runtime` suite, `pnpm lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, the dogfood battery, the other `dispatch-gates` families, a live server.

Must-fix: F1. Follow-up material (one card under #32560): F2, F3, F4, F5. F6 is a text fix that can ride the F1 push.

Implemented-by: `session_01Utp6CXsZN7qMreCTYFeT5Y`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgVSjQBHNkZd6Eqx2XX`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `24eb537614f6d80646e302a4bfcd816c874da902`
Local-runs: probe — round 2 (delta) on this head was dispatched to re-run the r1 door + database measurement, one ablation and the package suites, which the diff and check-runs alone cannot answer; runs listed under "Runs" below
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-action-slots.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts + none outside the diff that the hunks make a claim about (read only: packages/metadata/src/loaders/filesystem-loader.ts and remote-loader.ts, for the "every loader" claim; .changeset/32560-bare-action-read-loader-slots.md for the declaration lines, the BREAKING block and the ADR-0087 marker)

Round 2, delta on round 1 (6824229959, head `a309114bf`, FAIL on F1). Diff read at the merge base `cac0f1aab` (`git diff origin/main...24eb53761`: 13 files, +872/−87). Focus: the F1 fix `24eb53761` and the merge `d500fe858`. F2–F5 are on follow-up #32738 and are not re-judged; where the fix moved one, it is said below.

### ① Derived judgments

**F1 is closed.** Measured at this head with my own probe (not the PR's pins), a real `DatabaseLoader` over a row driver plus a door `MemoryLoader`:

| shape | before `unregister('action', NAME)` | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| r1's boot: door `[A]`, rows `[A, env]`, registry A + env; env on another object | bare read `env` | door `[A]`, rows `[A]`, list `[alpha]`, bare read `alpha`, a manager over the door alone answers `alpha` |
| same, env object-less | same | same |
| the door holding A and a copy of env | door `[A, env]` | door `[A]`, rows `[A]` |
| two nodes over one database, a door each, removal on node A (loader cache off) | both nodes read `env` | rows `[A]`; both doors `[A]`; both nodes read `alpha`, list `[alpha]` |

In r1 the first row gave door `[]`. The peer's door now keeps A through `removeNodeLocalCopies` → `deleteMetaItemFromLoader(loader, type, name, removal)`.

**The carry, read in the code.** `storeRemovalKeys` returns `packagelessOnly: true` only on its package-less-only arm (an action name, package-less slots beside a package's). `removalOf` judges the registry ∪ loaders view and passes the flag on; `unregisterAt` builds one scope (`{ packageId }`, else `{ packagelessOnly: true }`, else `{}`) and gives the same scope to every loader delete and to the cluster payload. `unregisterPackage` always names its package for a slotted type, so it never meets the new arm.

**Every `MetadataLoader` in the tree.**

- `MemoryLoader.delete`, `DatabaseLoader.delete`: honour the option; `packageId` wins when both are sent (measured on `MemoryLoader`; the manager never sends both).
- `FilesystemLoader`, `RemoteLoader`: no `delete`, and neither is a removal target (`isRemovalTarget`: a writable `datasource:` loader or a `memory:` loader with `delete`).
- No production loader outside `packages/metadata` implements the interface. The loaders that ignore the option are test doubles holding one item per name (`SharedStoreLoader` and the doubles in the delete-contract, invalidate-order, notify and objectql conformance tests); none can hold a package's slot beside a package-less one.
- A third-party loader that ignores the option deletes by its own rule, which is what it did on `main`; the PR body says so.

**A delete with no option.** Measured on `MemoryLoader`: A alone → every slot; the environment's item alone → every slot; A and B → refused (`PackageScopedNameRefusedError`); `{ packageId: B }` → B's only. These are `main`'s answers. The one shape that differs from `main` with no option is a single store holding A and a package-less slot (takes the package-less only), which is row 5b and was in r1's head.

**The payload.** Measured on a peer whose door holds A alone: `{ packagelessOnly: true }` → door `[A]`; `{}` → `[]` (by name, as `main`); `{ packageId: A }` → `[]`; `{ packageId: B }` → `[A]`; `packagelessOnly` of `false`, `null`, `'true'`, or `true` beside a `packageId` → dropped, door `[A]`; no `removal` key → `[A]`.

**Ablation** (one, restored, `git status` empty): `MemoryLoader.delete` ignoring `packagelessOnly` → 4 failed / 635 passed in the match-endpoint and cluster files (the door + database pin ×2, the direct loader pin, the two-node pin). Agrees with the body's count for that ablation.

**The merge `d500fe858`.** No conflict (`git show --remerge-diff` empty). Five files were changed on both sides. For four of them the patch each side made is byte-for-byte the patch it made before the merge (`git patch-id`: `package-scoped-resolution.ts`, `metadata-manager.ts`, `package-slotted-store.ts`, `metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts`). `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` has adjacent hunks, so the ids differ; read by hand, both import sets are kept. `main`'s side at head, read: `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` holds `picklist`, `mapping`, `dataset` (#31700); `environmentStoreKey`, `storedRowMemberOf`, `STORED_MEMBER_MAX_LENGTH`, `historyAddressOf`, the `slot` argument of `writeRegistryEntry` and the addressed `getHistory` / `rollback` / `diff` (#32569) are present and unchanged. The PR's package-less-only arm is keyed on `OWNER_KEYED_SLOT_TYPES` (action), so the three new slotted types keep `main`'s removal rule. `DatabaseLoader.delete` with the option deletes every row of the name's package-less slot, which fits #32540's row per member.

Findings:

- **F7 · should-fix (a shape the rows do not name; in r1's code, not seen in r1).** Row 5b names "A + environment on another object or object-less". Where a package-less row sits on the SAME object as A's (rows `[A, package-less]` on `account`, the door and the registry holding A), measured: the bare read answers `alpha` before and after (on one binding the package's slot answers, as on `main`), and `unregister('action', NAME)` resolves, deletes the package-less row and keeps A in the rows, the door and the registry. On `main` that call removed both. So in this shape the removal does not remove what the bare read answers (changeset §4's heading, the body's 速读 line), and the moved answer has no row and no pin. Where the registry's A slot was filled from such a package-less body (`registerInMemory` on A's binding), the registry keeps answering that body after its row is gone. `register` cannot produce the shape: I measured both orders (environment first, A first) and an environment-addressed rollback; each leaves one row, A's. It needs rows written before the per-package row or outside the loader. No loss against `main` (the removal takes less).
